paragraphs: The use of the words "we," "us" or "our" refers to American Healthcare REIT, Inc. and its subsidiaries, including American Healthcare REIT Holdings, LP, except where otherwise noted.

American Healthcare REIT, Inc., a Maryland corporation, is a self-managed real estate investment trust, or REIT, that acquires, owns and operates a diversified portfolio of clinical healthcare real estate properties, focusing primarily on senior housing, skilled nursing facilities, or SNFs, outpatient medical, or OM, buildings and other healthcare-related facilities. We have built a fully-integrated management platform, with approximately 121 employees as of December 31, 2025, that operates clinical healthcare properties throughout the United States, and in the United Kingdom and the Isle of Man. We own and operate our integrated senior health campuses, or ISHC, and senior-housing operating properties, or SHOP, utilizing the structure permitted by the REIT Investment Diversification and Empowerment Act of 2007, which is commonly referred to as a "RIDEA" structure. We have also originated and acquired secured loans and may acquire other real estate-related investments in the future on an infrequent and opportunistic basis. We generally seek investments that produce current income; however, we have selectively developed, and may continue to selectively develop, healthcare real estate properties. We have elected to be taxed as a REIT for U.S. federal income tax purposes. We believe that we have been organized and operated, and we intend to continue to operate, in conformity with the requirements for qualification and taxation as a REIT under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, or the Code.

We conduct substantially all of our operations through American Healthcare REIT Holdings, LP, or our operating partnership, and we are the sole general partner of our operating partnership. As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, we owned 99.0% and 98.7%, respectively, of the operating partnership units, or OP units, in our operating partnership, and the remaining 1.0% and 1.3% of the OP units, respectively, were owned by the following limited partners: (i) AHI Group Holdings, LLC, which is owned and controlled by Jeffrey T. Hanson, our Chairman of the Board of Directors and Interim Chief Executive Officer and President, Danny Prosky, our Chief Executive Officer, President and director, who, as previously disclosed, is currently taking a leave of absence from his executive role for medical reasons, and Mathieu B. Streiff, one of our non-executive directors; and (ii) a wholly-owned subsidiary of Griffin Capital Company, LLC. See Note 11, Redeemable Noncontrolling Interests, and Note 12, Equity — Noncontrolling Interests in Total Equity, to the Consolidated Financial Statements that are a part of this Annual Report on Form 10-K, for a further discussion of the ownership in our operating partnership.

On February 9, 2024, pursuant to a Registration Statement filed with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission, or SEC, on Form S-11 (File No. 333-267464), as amended, we closed our underwritten public offering, or the February 2024 Offering, through which we issued 64,400,000 shares of Common Stock, for a total of $772,800,000 in gross offering proceeds. Such amounts include the exercise in full of the underwriters' overallotment option to purchase up to an additional 8,400,000 shares of Common Stock. We listed these shares of Common Stock on the New York Stock Exchange, or NYSE, under the trading symbol "AHR" and began trading on February 7, 2024.

Following the closing of the February 2024 Offering and until August 5, 2024, we presented our Common Stock, Class T common stock and Class I common stock, as separate classes of common stock within our consolidated balance sheets and consolidated statements of equity. Any references to Common Stock in this Annual Report on Form 10-K refer to our NYSE-listed shares of common stock, whereas Class T common stock and Class I common stock refer to our historical non-listed shares of common stock. This applies to all historical periods presented herein. On August 5, 2024, 180 days after the listing of our Common Stock on the NYSE, each share of our Class T common stock and Class I common stock automatically converted into one share of our listed Common Stock.
See Note 12, Equity — Common Stock, to the Consolidated Financial Statements that are a part of this Annual Report on Form 10-K, for a further discussion of our public offerings.

Our principal executive offices are located at 18191 Von Karman Avenue, Suite 300, Irvine, California 92612, and our telephone number is (949) 270-9200. We maintain a website at www.AmericanHealthcareREIT.com, at which there is additional information about us. The contents of that site are not incorporated by reference in, or otherwise a part of, this filing. We make our periodic and current reports and all amendments to those reports available at www.AmericanHealthcareREIT.com as soon as reasonably practicable after such materials are electronically filed with the SEC. They also are available for printing by any stockholder upon request. In addition, copies of our filings with the SEC may be obtained from the SEC's website, https://www.SEC.gov. Access to these filings is free of charge.

Our business objectives are to grow our earnings and cash flows, maintain financial flexibility, increase the value of our portfolio, make regular cash distributions to our stockholders and generate attractive risk-adjusted returns through the following growth strategies:
• external growth through disciplined and targeted acquisitions to expand our diversified portfolio;
• continue to selectively develop and expand ISHC with experienced development partners;

• continue to generate strong organic growth in our long-term care portfolio comprised of ISHC and SHOP, as a result of historically low levels of new supply and ever increasing demand from an aging population; and
• actively position our balance sheet for growth.

We have acquired, and may continue to acquire, properties either directly or jointly with third parties and may also consider disposing of non-core properties from time to time. We generally seek investments that produce current income; however, we have selectively developed, are currently developing (through Trilogy Investors, LLC, or Trilogy), and may continue to selectively develop, real estate properties. Our portfolio may include properties in various stages of development other than those producing current income. These stages include unimproved land both with and without entitlements and permits, property to be redeveloped and repositioned, newly constructed properties and properties in lease-up or other stabilization stages, all of which have limited or no relevant operating histories and current income. We make such investment determinations based upon a variety of factors, including the anticipated risk-adjusted returns for such properties when compared with other available properties, the appropriate diversification of our portfolio and our objectives of realizing both current income and capital appreciation.

We seek to grow our earnings and cash flows, maintain financial flexibility, increase the value of our portfolio, make regular cash distributions and generate attractive risk-adjusted returns for our stockholders through the business objectives and growth strategies discussed above. In order to achieve these objectives, we may invest using a number of investment structures, which may include direct acquisitions, joint ventures, leveraged investments, issuing securities for property and direct and indirect investments in real estate. In order to maintain our exemption from regulation as an investment company under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended, or the Investment Company Act, we may be required to limit our investments in certain types of real estate-related investments. See "Investment Company Act Considerations" below for a further discussion.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Financial Results
The financial deterioration, insolvency or bankruptcy of one or more of our major tenants, operators, borrowers or other obligors could have a material adverse effect on us.
We are dependent on tenants for our revenue, and lease defaults or terminations could reduce our ability to make distributions to our stockholders.
We have experienced net losses in the past and we may experience additional losses in the future.
Our financial results and our ability to make distributions to our stockholders are subject to international, national and local market conditions we cannot control or predict.
Our investments in, and acquisitions of, senior housing, SNFs, OM buildings and other healthcare-related facilities may be unsuccessful or fail to meet our expectations.
If we cannot obtain debt or equity funding on favorable terms, our ability to acquire properties may be impaired or delayed, which could have a material adverse effect on us.
We may incur additional costs in re-leasing properties with specialized uses, which could materially and adversely affect us.
A breach of, or failure in, information technology systems on which we rely could materially and adversely impact us.
Risks Related to Investments in Real Estate
Changing market conditions could lead our real estate investments to decrease in value or may cause us to sell our properties at a loss in the future.
Most of our costs, such as operating and general and administrative expenses, interest expense and real estate acquisition and construction costs, are subject to inflation and may not be recoverable.
Our high concentrations of properties in particular geographic areas magnify the effects of negative conditions affecting those geographic areas.
Our buildings that are subject to ground leases could restrict our use of such facilities.
Our use of property-level rent coverages to measure our tenant's ability to make rent payments may not be accurate.

Terrorist attacks, acts of violence or war, political protests and unrest or public health crises have affected and may affect the markets in which we operate and have a material adverse effect on us.
Our business, tenants, residents and operators may face litigation and experience rising liability and insurance costs, which may materially and adversely affect us.
Inaccuracies in our underwriting assumptions and/or delays in the selection, acquisition, expansion or development of real properties may materially and adversely affect us.
We face possible liability for environmental cleanup costs and damages for contamination related to properties we acquire, which could materially and adversely affect us.
Our current and future properties and our tenants may be unable to compete successfully, which could result in lower rent payments and could materially and adversely affect us.
Ownership of property outside the United States may subject us to different or greater risks than those associated with our domestic operations.
paragraphs: Investing in our Common Stock involves risks. Our stockholders should carefully consider the risk factors below, together with all of the other information included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our Consolidated Financial Statements and the notes thereto included herein. If any of these risks were to occur, our business, financial condition, liquidity, results of operations and prospects and our ability to service our debt and make distributions to our stockholders at a particular rate, or at all, could be materially and adversely affected (which we refer to collectively as "materially and adversely affecting us" or having "a material adverse effect on us" and comparable phrases).
Below is a summary of the principal factors that make an investment in our Common Stock speculative or risky. This summary should be read in conjunction with the full risk factors contained below.
Risks Related to Our Business and Financial Results
• The financial deterioration, insolvency or bankruptcy of one or more of our major tenants, operators, borrowers or other obligors could have a material adverse effect on us.
• We are dependent on tenants for our revenue, and lease defaults or terminations could reduce our ability to make distributions to our stockholders.
• We have experienced net losses in the past and we may experience additional losses in the future.

American Healthcare REIT, Inc. 為馬裏蘭州公司，為一自營的不動產投資信託，或 REIT，專門取得、擁有並營運多元化之臨牀醫療不動產資產，主要聚焦於長照機構、專業護理機構、或 SNFs、門診醫療、或 OM 建築物及其他醫療相關設施。我們已建立一完整的管理平台，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，約有 121 名員工，於美國、英國及曼島營運臨牀醫療不動產。我們擁有並營運我們整合的長照健康校區，或 ISHC，以及長照機構營運不動產，或 SHOP，利用 2007 年 REIT 投資多元化與賦權法案所允許的結構，通常稱為 "RIDEA" 結構。我們亦已發起並取得抵押貸款，未來可能在罕見且機會出現時取得其他不動產相關投資。我們一般尋求產生現金收入之投資；然而，我們已選擇性地開發，並可能繼續選擇性地開發醫療不動產。

我們透過 American Healthcare REIT Holdings, LP，或我們的營運合夥企業，進行幾乎所有營運活動，我們為營運合夥企業的唯一普通合夥人。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日，我們擁有營運合夥企業單位，或 OP 單位，分別為 99.0% 及 98.7%，營運合夥企業單位，或 OP 單位，分別為 1.0% 及 1.3%，由以下有限合夥人擁有：(i) AHI Group Holdings, LLC，由 Jeffrey T. Hanson 所擁有及控制，為我們董事會主席及臨時首席執行官及總裁，Danny Prosky，為我們首席執行官、總裁及董事，先前已披露，目前因醫療原因暫停執行職務，以及 Mathieu B. Streiff，為我們非執行董事之一；以及 (ii) Griffin Capital Company, LLC 的全資子公司。請參閱本年度報告 10-K 所附財務報表之附註 11，可贖回非控制性權益，以及附註 12，權益 — 非控制性權益於總權益中，以進一步討論我們營運合夥企業之股權。

2024 年 2 月 9 日，根據向美國證券交易委員會，或 SEC，提交的註冊聲明，於 Form S-11（檔案編號 333-267464）中，我們完成經認購的公開發行，或 2024 年 2 月發行，發行 64,400,000 股普通股，總計取得 772,800,000 美元之發行總額。此金額包含經認購的經理人過量認購權，以購買最多 8,400,000 股普通股。我們於紐約證券交易所，或 NYSE，以 "AHR" 為交易代碼上市這些普通股，並於 2024 年 2 月 7 日開始交易。

在 2024 年 2 月發行完成後，直至 2024 年 8 月 5 日，我們於合併資產負債表及合併權益表中，將普通股、Class T 普通股及 Class I 普通股，作為我們普通股之不同類別。本年度報告 10-K 中任何提及普通股之參考，均指我們於紐約證券交易所上市之普通股，而 Class T 普通股及 Class I 普通股則指我們歷史上的非上市普通股。此適用於本報告中所有歷史時期。2024 年 8 月 5 日，自我們普通股於紐約證券交易所上市後 180 天，我們 Class T 普通股及 Class I 普通股每 shares 自動轉換為 1 shares 之上市普通股。
請參閱本年度報告 10-K 所附財務報表之附註 12，權益 — 普通股，以進一步討論我們之公開發行。

我們的總部位於加州爾灣市 Von Karman 大道 18191 號，300 號套房，電話為 (949) 270-9200。我們維護網站 www.AmericanHealthcareREIT.com，提供更多關於我們的資訊。該網站內容並未被引用為本檔的一部分。我們會在 SEC 電子檔上傳後盡速於 www.AmericanHealthcareREIT.com 提供我們的定期及現金報告與所有修正後的報告，股東亦可請求列印這些報告。此外，我們的 SEC 檔案亦可於 SEC 網站 https://www.SEC.gov 獲取。這些檔的存取為免費。
我們的業務目標為成長我們的獲利與現金流、維持財務彈性、提高我們資產組合的價值、定期向股東發放現金分紅，並透過以下成長策略產生有吸引力的風險調整後回報：
• 透過嚴謹且具針對性的收購活動來實現外部成長，以擴展我們多元化的資產組合;
• 繼續選擇性地開發與擴展ISHC，並與具經驗的開發夥伴合作;
• 繼續在長期照護資產組閤中產生強勁的內在成長，該組合包含ISHC與SHOP，這是因為歷史上新供應量極低，而人口老化所導致的需求持續增加所致; 和
• 主動地將我們的資產負債表定位為支持成長;

我們已取得，並可能繼續取得，不動產，可能是直接或與第三方共同取得，同時也可能會考慮不時處置非核心資產。我們通常尋求能產生現金收入的投資；然而，我們已選擇性地開發，目前正透過Trilogy Investors, LLC，或Trilogy進行開發，並可能繼續選擇性地開發不動產。我們的資產組合可能包含處於不同開發階段的不動產，這些不動產可能不產生現金收入。這些階段包括有或沒有權利與許可的未開發土地、待重新開發與重新定位的不動產、新建的不動產以及處於租賃期或其它穩定階段的不動產，這些不動產均具有有限或無相關營運歷史及現金收入。我們做出這些投資決定是根據多種因素，包括這些不動產與其他可選不動產相比的預期風險調整後回報、我們資產組合的適當分散化，以及我們實現現金收入與資本增值的目標。

我們尋求透過上述商業目標與成長策略來增加我們的獲利與現金流，維持財務彈性，提高資產組合價值，定期發放現金分紅，並為股東產生有吸引力的風險調整後回報。為達成這些目標，我們可能使用多種投資結構，這些結構可能包括直接收購、合資企業、槓桿投資、發行證券以取得不動產，以及直接與間接投資於不動產。為維持我們根據1940年投資公司法（已修正）或投資公司法而免除投資公司規範的資格，我們可能需要限制某些類型的不動產相關投資。有關投資公司法考量的進一步討論，請參閱下方的『投資公司法考量』部分。

headings: 與我們業務及財務結果相關的風險
我們主要租戶、營運者、借款人或其他義務人之財務惡化、破產或清算，可能對我們產生重大不利影響。
我們依賴租戶來產生收入，租賃違約或終止可能降低我們向股東發放紅利的能力。
我們過去曾出現淨虧損，未來也可能出現更多虧損。
我們的財務結果及向股東發放紅利的能力，受國際、國家及地方市場條件影響，而這些條件我們無法控制或預測。
我們對高齡住宅、護理機構、營運管理大樓及其他醫療相關設施之投資及收購，可能無法成功或未達我們預期。
若我們無法以有利條件取得債務或權益融資，我們取得不動產的能力可能受影響或延宕，這可能對我們產生重大不利影響。
我們可能因重新出租具特殊用途的不動產而產生額外成本，這可能會對我們造成重大且不利的影響。
我們所依賴的資訊科技系統若發生違約或故障，可能會對我們造成重大且不利的影響。
與投資不動產相關的風險
市場條件的變化可能導致我們的不動產投資價值下降，或可能導致我們未來以虧損價格出售不動產。
我們的大部分成本，例如營運及一般及行政費用、利息費用以及不動產取得及建設成本，均受通貨膨脹影響，且可能無法收回。
我們在特定地理區域的不動產集中度較高，這會放大這些地理區域負面條件的影響。
我們的不動產若涉及地面租賃，可能會限制我們對這些設施的使用。
我們使用不動產層級的租金覆蓋率來衡量租戶支付租金的能力，可能並不準確。
恐怖攻擊、暴力事件或戰爭、政治抗爭與動亂或公共衛生危機已影響並可能影響我們所從事的市場，並可能對我們造成重大不利影響。
我們的業務、租戶、居民及營運者可能面臨訴訟，並可能遭遇負擔增加與保險成本上升，這可能對我們造成重大且不利的影響。
我們在風險評估假設上的不準確，或在選擇、取得、擴張或開發實物資產時的延誤，可能對我們造成重大且不利的影響。
我們可能因取得的不動產所涉及的環境清理成本與污染損害而面臨責任，這可能對我們造成重大且不利的影響。
我們目前及未來的不動產與租戶可能無法成功競爭，這可能導致租金支付減少，並可能對我們造成重大且不利的影響。
擁有美國境外的不動產可能使我們面臨與國內營運不同的或更高的風險。
paragraphs: 投資本公司普通股涉及風險。本公司股東應謹慎考慮下列風險因素，並配合本年度報告表10-K所包含的所有其他資訊，包括本公司合併財務報表及其附註。若上述任何風險發生，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、流動性、營運成果與前景，以及本公司償還債務及對股東進行分紅的能力造成重大且不利的影響（我們 collectively 稱為 "重大且不利影響" 或 "對本公司造成重大不利影響"，並包含類似用語）。
下列為使投資本公司普通股成為投機或高風險因素的主要因素摘要。此摘要應配合下列完整風險因素一併閱讀。
與本公司業務及財務結果相關的風險
